section_title: Selective Vulnerability of SST Interneurons in Aging and Neurodegeneration
thesis: The somatostatin signal declines with normal ageing by roughly the same magnitude that disease cohorts report, and declines again after almost every experimental insult - but the studies that count cells independently of the peptide, and the studies that delete the proposed vulnerability mechanisms, do not support a simple account of SST neurons as intrinsically fragile. Vulnerability in this literature is better described as region- and insult-specific than as a property of the cell class.
scope_notes: Cross-disease and aging vulnerability mechanisms; separates loss of SST cells from loss of the peptide or marker.

arg_01.thesis: Age-related decline of the somatostatin signal - Establish the ageing baseline across species: large transcript and peptide reductions in aged rodent and primate brain, set against cell-count studies in the same aged tissue that report little or no loss. Make the quantitative point that ageing alone produces marker reductions of the same size that disease cohorts attribute to pathology, so age matching is not a methodological nicety.

arg_02.thesis: The hilar lesion model and what it does and does not generalise - Treat hilar SST cell loss after seizure and ischaemia as the strongest demonstration of SST-cell vulnerability anywhere in the literature, then bound it: the same class is spared in diffuse TBI with axotomy restricted to PV cells, and is preserved in striatum under hypoxic-ischaemic insult.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_01.thesis: Whether somatostatin-immunoreactive neuron density is actually reduced in Alzheimer-type dementia cortex. One study reports fewer SST interneurons per mm2 in AD temporal cortex; the other reports no reduction in neocortical SST cell density in senile dementia of the Alzheimer type, attributing change to fibre terminals instead.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_01.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_01 (foreground; resolution_status=open). The founding disagreement of the whole field: is SST-immunoreactive neuron density actually reduced in Alzheimer-type cortex, or is the pathology in the fibres? Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_03.thesis: Aging rat cortex: somatostatin transcript measures fall by 49-80% while immunohistochemical counts of somatostatin-positive cells in the same aging rodent cortex decline only slightly. The discrepancy separates transcript downregulation in surviving neurons from actual cell loss.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_03.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_03 (foreground; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Transcript falls 49-80% while immunohistochemical counts barely move in the same aged rodent cortex - the cleanest available dissociation of downregulation from death. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_08.thesis: Whether the absence of cytosolic calcium-binding proteins explains the selective vulnerability of hilar somatostatin neurons. The correlative study links lack of PV/calbindin to vulnerability, but genetic deletion of these buffers produces no interneuron loss or morphological abnormality, undercutting a simple buffer-deficiency account.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_08.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_08 (foreground; resolution_status=open). Genetic deletion of the calcium buffers whose absence is said to explain SST vulnerability produces no interneuron loss, undercutting the dominant cell-intrinsic account. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_04.thesis: Whether SST interneurons are the vulnerable or the resilient class after insult. Epilepsy models show hilar SST interneurons reduced to 18% of control, whereas diffuse traumatic brain injury spares SST axons (axotomy largely restricted to parvalbumin cells) and enhances SST output. Vulnerability therefore appears insult-specific rather than an intrinsic property of the class.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_04.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_04 (foreground; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). SST cells are the vulnerable class in epilepsy and the spared class in diffuse TBI; establishes insult-specificity over class-intrinsic fragility. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): model_construct_and_species_transfer.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_02.thesis: Magnitude of SST neuron loss in Alzheimer's disease: stereological counts give a 50% reduction in hippocampus, whereas immunohistochemical counts in cortex find no difference between aged controls and AD. The studies differ in region (hippocampus vs cortex) and in whether design-based stereology was used.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_02.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_02 (integrated; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Stereology in hippocampus versus density counts in cortex give 50% loss versus none. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_05.thesis: Direction of somatostatin change across neurodegenerative diseases: somatostatin content is elevated two- to threefold in Huntington disease basal ganglia, while somatostatin-positive cell density is reduced in Parkinson disease amygdala. Peptide content and cell density are measured by different assays, so the cross-disease contrast may be assay- as well as disease-driven.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_05.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_05 (integrated; resolution_status=open). Opposite directions of somatostatin change across diseases measured by different assays; sets up sec-huntingtons and sec-parkinsons-lewy-body. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_06.thesis: Whether somatostatin-containing neurons are intrinsically vulnerable or intrinsically resistant to excitotoxic/ischemic insult. In hippocampal dentate hilus they are the first population lost, whereas in striatum under hypoxic-ischemic insult somatostatin and NPY levels are preserved while other markers fall. The disagreement tracks brain region and circuit context rather than the marker itself.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_06.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_06 (integrated; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Same marker, opposite vulnerability verdicts in hilus versus striatum. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_07.thesis: Whether amyloid pathology causes loss of hippocampal somatostatin interneurons or only functional impairment of a numerically intact population. The overexpression model reports dysfunction of O-LM interneurons, while the knock-in model finds unchanged SOM interneuron density even at 24 months.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_07.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_07 (integrated; resolution_status=open). Overexpression model reports O-LM dysfunction while knock-in reports unchanged density at 24 months; previews the construct-dosage theme. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): model_construct_and_species_transfer.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_09.thesis: Whether traumatic brain injury produces a consistent, quantifiable depletion of somatostatin interneurons. Controlled cortical impact yields significant ipsilateral SST interneuron loss and afferent disconnection, whereas lateral fluid percussion injury yields heterogeneous hippocampal changes and no obvious cortical interneuron loss.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_09.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_09 (integrated; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Two TBI models disagree on whether SST depletion is consistent and quantifiable. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_unanchored.thesis: The somatostatin signal declines with normal ageing by roughly the same magnitude that disease cohorts report, and declines again after almost every experimental insult - but the studies that count cells independently of the peptide, and the studies that delete the proposed vulnerability mechanisms, do not support a simple account of SST neurons as intrinsically fragile. Vulnerability in this literature is better described as region- and insult-specific than as a property of the cell class.

subsections.title: Age-related decline of the somatostatin signal
subsections.job: Establish the ageing baseline across species: large transcript and peptide reductions in aged rodent and primate brain, set against cell-count studies in the same aged tissue that report little or no loss. Make the quantitative point that ageing alone produces marker reductions of the same size that disease cohorts attribute to pathology, so age matching is not a methodological nicety.

subsections.title: The hilar lesion model and what it does and does not generalise
subsections.job: Treat hilar SST cell loss after seizure and ischaemia as the strongest demonstration of SST-cell vulnerability anywhere in the literature, then bound it: the same class is spared in diffuse TBI with axotomy restricted to PV cells, and is preserved in striatum under hypoxic-ischaemic insult.

subsections.title: Candidate cell-intrinsic mechanisms and their evidential status
subsections.job: Evaluate the mechanistic menu - metabolic load, calcium-buffer deficiency, excitotoxic susceptibility, ER/oxidative stress from peptide precursor processing, BDNF dependence - against what was actually measured. The buffer-deficiency account is undercut by genetic deletion of PV and calbindin producing no interneuron loss; the metabolic account is a false-consensus risk with no per-cell-type measurement retrieved.

subsections.title: Cross-disease comparison of magnitude, and why the convergence is partly artefactual
subsections.job: Assemble the 20-80% depletion range across epilepsy, amyloid, genetic-injury and human AD tissue and show the magnitude tracks denominator and labelling strategy; flag that two entries count reporter-defined subsets rather than the whole population.

subsections.title: What would have to be true for the class-level claim to hold
subsections.job: Convert the section into a testable statement: the class-level vulnerability claim requires marker-independent counting in the same tissue in which the marker falls, and that experiment exists in rodents and not in humans.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cell-intrinsic metabolic load as the cause of SST interneuron vulnerability
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration that SST interneurons carry a higher metabolic or oxidative burden than neighbouring interneuron classes - the claim is repeated in reviews and inferred from transcriptomic associations, but no direct per-cell-type measurement of oxygen consumption, ATP demand or ROS load was recovered in these searches
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: a widely stated mechanistic explanation for selective vulnerability without traceable experimental evidence at the level of identified SST cells

evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: SST interneurons are defined partly by the absence of parvalbumin's calcium-buffering capacity, yet no study retrieved here measured calcium transients or buffering capacity in identified SST cells under degenerative conditions
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The buffering-deficit hypothesis is the main cell-intrinsic account of SST vulnerability and is currently supported only by inference from marker expression

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Separating SST neuron death from somatostatin downregulation
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Studies that report both a cell-identity-independent marker (e.g. fate-mapping, nuclear counts, snRNA-seq proportions) and peptide/mRNA levels in the same tissue; most aging and AD studies report only one, which is why transcript studies and cell-count studies disagree
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The entire selective-vulnerability claim depends on whether SST neurons die or merely stop expressing their peptide; the two have opposite therapeutic implications

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: BDNF dependence of SST interneuron survival in aging brain
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct loss-of-function evidence that reduced BDNF/TrkB signalling causes SST interneuron loss in the aged (rather than developing) brain; retrieved evidence is developmental culture work and correlated age-related co-decline of BDNF and SST transcripts
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Neurotrophin dependence is used to explain age-related SST decline but the causal link in aged tissue is untested in the retrieved literature

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cross-disease comparison of SST vulnerability with matched methods
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: A single study quantifying SST interneuron abundance across Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's and schizophrenia tissue with one method and one cell-type definition
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Cross-disease vulnerability claims currently rest on pooling radioimmunoassay, immunohistochemistry and transcriptomic proportion estimates from different eras, which the CSF and basal-ganglia discrepancies show is not safe

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Calcium-buffer deficiency as the mechanism of hilar SST neuron vulnerability
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: A causal test. The mechanism rests on the correlative observation that hilar SST cells lack parvalbumin and calbindin, while genetic deletion of these buffers produces no interneuron loss or morphological change, and parvalbumin content does not protect striatal interneurons from excitotoxin.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: false_consensus_risk: the buffer-deficiency account is widely repeated as the explanation for selective SST vulnerability but the available genetic test argues against it.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cell loss versus marker downregulation in SST interneuron depletion
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Studies that pair lineage-independent labelling (e.g. GAD67 reporter or genetic SST-lineage labelling) with peptide immunoreactivity in the same aged or diseased tissue. Most human and many animal reports quantify somatostatin immunoreactivity or transcript level, which cannot separate peptide loss from neuron loss; the one developmental-hypoxia study that did this attributed the apparent 32% SST decrease to reduced marker expression rather than cell death.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The entire selective-vulnerability inference for human cortex rests on marker-based measures, so the distinction determines whether SST interneurons die or fall silent.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Metabolic and ER-stress vulnerability in aging rather than stress or disease models
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct measurement of unfolded protein response or oxidative load in SST interneurons of aged animals. The ER-stress vulnerability mechanism was established under chronic psychosocial stress in young adults, and no equivalent measurement in aged or neurodegenerative tissue was retrieved.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The ER-stress account is the strongest available cell-intrinsic mechanism; whether it operates in aging is untested and therefore extrapolated.

Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Age-related decline of the somatostatin signal
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Establish the ageing baseline across species: large transcript and peptide reductions in aged rodent and primate brain, set against cell-count studies in the same aged tissue that report little or no loss. Make the quantitative point that ageing alone produces marker reductions of the same size that disease cohorts attribute to pathology, so age matching is not a methodological nicety.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: The hilar lesion model and what it does and does not generalise
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Treat hilar SST cell loss after seizure and ischaemia as the strongest demonstration of SST-cell vulnerability anywhere in the literature, then bound it: the same class is spared in diffuse TBI with axotomy restricted to PV cells, and is preserved in striatum under hypoxic-ischaemic insult.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Candidate cell-intrinsic mechanisms and their evidential status
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Evaluate the mechanistic menu - metabolic load, calcium-buffer deficiency, excitotoxic susceptibility, ER/oxidative stress from peptide precursor processing, BDNF dependence - against what was actually measured. The buffer-deficiency account is undercut by genetic deletion of PV and calbindin producing no interneuron loss; the metabolic account is a false-consensus risk with no per-cell-type measurement retrieved.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Cross-disease comparison of magnitude, and why the convergence is partly artefactual
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Assemble the 20-80% depletion range across epilepsy, amyloid, genetic-injury and human AD tissue and show the magnitude tracks denominator and labelling strategy; flag that two entries count reporter-defined subsets rather than the whole population.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: What would have to be true for the class-level claim to hold
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Convert the section into a testable statement: the class-level vulnerability claim requires marker-independent counting in the same tissue in which the marker falls, and that experiment exists in rodents and not in humans.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether somatostatin-immunoreactive neuron density is actually reduced in Alzheimer-type dementia cortex. One study reports fewer SST interneurons per mm2 in AD temporal cortex; the other reports no reduction in neocortical SST cell density in senile dementia of the Alzheimer type, attributing change to fibre terminals instead.

Aging rat cortex: somatostatin transcript measures fall by 49-80% while immunohistochemical counts of somatostatin-positive cells in the same aging rodent cortex decline only slightly. The discrepancy separates transcript downregulation in surviving neurons from actual cell loss.

Whether the absence of cytosolic calcium-binding proteins explains the selective vulnerability of hilar somatostatin neurons. The correlative study links lack of PV/calbindin to vulnerability, but genetic deletion of these buffers produces no interneuron loss or morphological abnormality, undercutting a simple buffer-deficiency account.

Whether SST interneurons are the vulnerable or the resilient class after insult. Epilepsy models show hilar SST interneurons reduced to 18% of control, whereas diffuse traumatic brain injury spares SST axons (axotomy largely restricted to parvalbumin cells) and enhances SST output. Vulnerability therefore appears insult-specific rather than an intrinsic property of the class.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict; group into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each rather than covering sequentially.
